tools.name: SparkLoop
tools.pricing: Free to join the Partner Network and Upscribe recommendation widget (SparkLoop takes a share of paid-recommendation earnings). Paying other newsletters to recommend you is a separate paid program.
tools.best_for: Getting paid recommendations and buying cross-newsletter referrals
tools.verdict: The best-known newsletter recommendation network. Earning from recommendations is low-risk; paying for referrals only makes sense once you know what a subscriber is worth to you.

tools.name: Supascribe
tools.pricing: Free for your first 100 subscribers captured and 1,000 embed views; a paid Pro plan after that (usage add-ons beyond plan limits).
tools.best_for: Writers with their own website who want on-brand Substack signup forms, popups and landing pages
tools.verdict: Fills a real gap: Substack's native embed is fixed-width and unstyled. Independent (not affiliated with Substack), and only useful if you drive traffic from a site you control.

tools.name: WriteStack
tools.pricing: Hobbyist $23.99/mo, Standard $32.99/mo, Enterprise $99.99/mo; 7-day free trial.
tools.best_for: Writers who live on Substack Notes and want batch scheduling, research and Notes-to-subscriber analytics
tools.verdict: The most complete Substack-only Notes suite. Pricey for a beginner, and publishing runs through a Chromium browser extension acting in your logged-in session.

tools.name: Narrareach
tools.pricing: From $19.99/mo ($199/yr); higher tiers $39/mo and $89/mo (discounted yearly).
tools.best_for: Turning long-form posts into Notes and cross-posting to LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Threads and Medium
tools.verdict: Good if distribution beyond Substack is your bottleneck. Hands Notes to Substack's native scheduler rather than posting from a stored session.

tools.name: StackSweller
tools.pricing: Pro $39/mo, or $25/mo billed yearly ($250/yr).
tools.best_for: A simple cloud queue for batch-scheduling Substack Notes
tools.verdict: Does one job (a Notes queue that runs with your laptop closed). Be aware it works by holding your Substack session, and Substack now schedules single Notes natively.

tools.name: Byline OS
tools.pricing: Starter free (CSV import, 30-day retention); Growth $19/mo; Scale $49/mo. 14-day trial. Currently in private beta.
tools.best_for: Paid-newsletter writers who want MRR, churn, cohort and revenue-per-post analytics
tools.verdict: Promising revenue-first analytics built specifically for Substack. It is a beta product; live sync uses your Substack session cookie and undocumented internal APIs, so the CSV-upload mode is the safer start.

tools.name: Google Analytics
tools.pricing: Free.
tools.best_for: Seeing where your Substack traffic comes from (Substack lets you add a GA measurement ID)
tools.verdict: Free and worth connecting on day one for referral sources. Overkill for most writers beyond the acquisition reports.

tools.name: Subshack
tools.pricing: Free (Subshack 1.0), including a no-signup public profile audit.
tools.best_for: Finding out which Notes and posts actually bring subscribers, and auditing your profile
tools.verdict: A free, measurement-first browser extension that never posts for you. New and small, so expect rough edges.

tools.name: Bitly
tools.pricing: Free (with ads); Core $10/mo (annual only); Growth $29/mo; Premium $199/mo (annual pricing).
tools.best_for: Tracking clicks on links you share to social, podcasts and print
tools.verdict: Handy for knowing which channel sends readers. The free tier is limited; many writers can get by with UTM tags plus Google Analytics.

tools.name: Plausible
tools.pricing: From $9/mo (Starter, 10k monthly pageviews); Growth $14/mo; Business $19/mo. Free trial.
tools.best_for: Privacy-friendly analytics for your own website or landing page
tools.verdict: Excellent lightweight analytics, but you can't install it on a substack.com publication. Use it on a personal site that funnels readers to Substack.

tools.name: Typefully
tools.pricing: Free (10 posts/mo); Creator $99/yr; Business $20 per social set/mo.
tools.pricing_source: official pricing page is JS-rendered; amounts from third-party pricing trackers checked Oct 2026
tools.best_for: X-first writers who also want to post to LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky and Substack Notes
tools.verdict: A polished writing-first scheduler with Substack Notes support. The free plan is enough to test it.

tools.name: Buffer
tools.pricing: Free (up to 3 channels); Essentials $5/channel/mo billed yearly ($6 monthly).
tools.best_for: Scheduling Notes alongside every other social channel from one calendar
tools.verdict: Reliable and affordable, and its free plan includes Substack Notes scheduling. The best default if you post to several networks.

tools.name: Hypefury
tools.pricing: From $6/mo (1 channel) to $19/mo (all channels); 7-day free trial.
tools.best_for: Automating evergreen reposts and growth on X
tools.verdict: Strong automation for X-heavy writers. Less relevant if X isn't where your readers are.

tools.name: Taplio
tools.pricing: Starter $39/mo; Growth $69/mo; Pro $199/mo; 7-day free trial.
tools.best_for: Writers growing a professional audience on LinkedIn
tools.verdict: Effective for LinkedIn but expensive. Only worth it if LinkedIn is a primary acquisition channel.

tools.name: Repurpose.io
tools.pricing: Starter $35/mo; Pro $79/mo; Agency $179/mo (cheaper yearly); 14-day free trial.
tools.best_for: Automatically distributing video and podcast clips across platforms
tools.verdict: Saves real time if you make video or audio. Pure text writers don't need it.

tools.name: Canva
tools.pricing: Free; Pro US$144/yr for one person (before tax).
tools.best_for: Header images, social graphics, Notes images and simple brand kits
tools.verdict: The default design tool for newsletter writers. The free plan covers most needs.
tools.notes: Affiliate: Canva Help Center page 'Become a Canva affiliate through the Canvassador Program'.

tools.name: Figma
tools.pricing: Free Starter; Professional full seat $16/mo.
tools.best_for: Custom visual systems, templates and detailed design work
tools.verdict: More power than most writers need. Pick it if you already know it or want pixel-level control.

tools.name: Kittl
tools.pricing: Free plan; paid Pro, Expert and Max plans (see pricing page).
tools.best_for: Typography-heavy graphics and AI-assisted illustrations
tools.verdict: A stylish Canva alternative with great type tools. The free plan is for personal use only.

tools.name: Unsplash
tools.pricing: Free to use under the Unsplash License.
tools.best_for: Free, high-quality photos for post headers
tools.verdict: The go-to free photo library. Popular images show up everywhere, so crop or edit them to stand out.

tools.name: remove.bg
tools.pricing: Free to try; paid plans for full-resolution output (see pricing page).
tools.best_for: One-click background removal for headshots and product images
tools.verdict: Fast and accurate. Now a Canva brand, and Canva Pro includes a background remover, so you may not need both.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.pricing: Free; Pro from $12/mo.
tools.best_for: Catching typos and clarity issues everywhere you write, including the Substack editor
tools.verdict: The free browser extension is worth installing. Pro's rewrites can flatten your voice, so accept suggestions selectively.

tools.name: Hemingway Editor
tools.pricing: Free web editor; Editor Plus from $8.33/mo billed annually ($100/yr).
tools.best_for: Making dense posts easier to read
tools.verdict: The free web version does the core job (highlighting long and passive sentences). Most writers don't need Plus.

tools.name: ProWritingAid
tools.pricing: Free; Premium $10/mo billed yearly ($120) or $30/mo monthly.
tools.best_for: Deep style reports for long-form and fiction writers
tools.verdict: More thorough reports than Grammarly. Worth trying if you write long essays or serialized fiction.

tools.name: LanguageTool
tools.pricing: Free; Premium $24.90/mo monthly or $69.90/yr.
tools.pricing_source: LanguageTool help center + third-party price tracker
tools.best_for: Multilingual writers and anyone who wants a Grammarly alternative
tools.verdict: Strong grammar checking across many languages, and much cheaper per year than monthly billing.

tools.name: QuillBot
tools.pricing: Free; Premium $19.95/mo or $99.95/yr.
tools.best_for: Paraphrasing, summarizing and quick rewrites
tools.verdict: Useful for tightening a stubborn paragraph. Don't lean on it for whole posts, because readers subscribe for your voice.

tools.name: Notion
tools.pricing: Free; Plus $10/seat/mo.
tools.best_for: Editorial calendars, idea banks and sponsor CRMs
tools.verdict: The most flexible planning hub for newsletter writers. The free plan covers solo use.

tools.name: Trello
tools.pricing: Free (up to 10 collaborators); Standard $5/user/mo billed annually.
tools.best_for: A simple kanban for drafts moving from idea to published
tools.verdict: Simpler than Notion if you only need a board. Free is plenty for one writer.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.pricing: Free; optional Sync $4/mo and Publish $8/mo (billed annually).
tools.best_for: Building a personal knowledge base of notes, quotes and ideas
tools.verdict: Great for writers who think in linked notes. Your files stay local in Markdown.

tools.name: Readwise
tools.pricing: Readwise Full $9.99/mo billed annually ($12.99 monthly); Lite $5.59/mo billed annually.
tools.best_for: Collecting highlights from books and articles to feed your writing
tools.verdict: A strong research engine for essayists and curators. Its Reader app is included with Full.

tools.name: Google Trends
tools.pricing: Free.
tools.best_for: Checking whether a topic is rising before you write about it
tools.verdict: A quick, free sanity check for timely topics and post titles.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.pricing: Free; Professional from $19.99/mo.
tools.best_for: Automating busywork such as logging new posts to a spreadsheet or sending sponsor reminders
tools.verdict: Powerful glue between apps. Substack has no official public API, so automations usually start from its RSS feed or email.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.pricing: Free; Plus $20/mo.
tools.best_for: Brainstorming angles, outlines, headlines and research summaries
tools.verdict: A versatile thinking partner. Use it for ideas and edits rather than finished prose your readers will recognize as generic.

tools.name: Claude
tools.pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo or $17/mo billed annually.
tools.best_for: Long-document feedback, structural edits and drafting help
tools.verdict: Particularly good at critiquing long drafts. The same caution about voice applies.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo.
tools.pricing_source: Perplexity pricing hub + third-party price tracker
tools.best_for: Quick research with cited sources
tools.verdict: Faster than a search engine for background research. Always click through and verify the citations.

tools.name: Sudowrite
tools.pricing: Hobby & Student $10/mo; Professional $22/mo; Max $44/mo; free trial.
tools.best_for: Fiction writers publishing serialized stories
tools.verdict: Purpose-built for fiction. Not the right tool for essays or news-style newsletters.

tools.name: Descript
tools.pricing: Free; Hobbyist $16/mo billed annually ($24 monthly); Creator $24/mo annually ($35 monthly).
tools.best_for: Editing podcast and video by editing the transcript
tools.verdict: The easiest way for writers to edit audio and video. A natural fit for Substack podcasts.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.pricing: Free (10k credits/mo); Starter $6/mo; Creator $22/mo; higher tiers available.
tools.best_for: Producing audio versions of posts with natural-sounding AI voices
tools.verdict: Best-in-class AI voice. Tell listeners when a voice is synthetic.

tools.name: Riverside
tools.pricing: Free; Pro $24/mo billed annually ($288/yr).
tools.best_for: Recording remote interviews in high quality
tools.verdict: Records each guest locally, so remote interviews sound studio-grade. Ideal for interview-driven newsletters.

tools.name: Audacity
tools.pricing: Free and open source.
tools.best_for: Recording and cleaning up voiceovers on a zero budget
tools.verdict: Dated interface but free and capable for simple narration edits.

tools.name: Adobe Podcast
tools.pricing: Free tier; premium features require a paid Adobe plan (check site for current offer).
tools.pricing_source: official site; premium-plan details from third-party reports
tools.best_for: Making laptop-mic recordings sound clean (Enhance Speech)
tools.verdict: Enhance Speech is impressive on the free tier. Check Adobe's current plans before relying on premium features.

tools.name: OpusClip
tools.pricing: Free (60 credits/mo); Starter $15/mo; Pro $14.50/mo billed annually.
tools.best_for: Turning long videos or podcast episodes into short social clips
tools.verdict: Fast way to get shorts from long recordings. Review the AI's clip choices before posting.

tools.name: Tally
tools.pricing: Free (unlimited forms and submissions); Pro $24/mo; Business $74/mo.
tools.best_for: Reader surveys, sponsor inquiry forms and feedback forms
tools.verdict: The most generous free form builder. Substack posts can't host forms directly, so link to it from your post or About page.

tools.name: Datawrapper
tools.pricing: Free; Pro $21/user/mo; Business $39/user/mo.
tools.best_for: Clean, accurate charts, maps and tables for data-driven posts
tools.verdict: Newsroom-quality charts for free. In Substack, the reliable route is exporting a PNG and linking to the interactive version.

tools.name: Flourish
tools.pricing: Free (public publishing with attribution); paid Presenter (via Canva Business) and Publisher/Enterprise plans on contract.
tools.best_for: Animated and interactive charts and scrollytelling
tools.verdict: More dramatic visuals than Datawrapper. Same Substack caveat: plan on a static image plus a link.

tools.name: Linktree
tools.pricing: Free; Starter $6/mo annually ($8 monthly); Pro $12/mo; Premium $30/mo.
tools.best_for: A link-in-bio page that points social followers to your Substack
tools.verdict: Fine for bios, but your Substack homepage can often serve as the link. Only pay if you need the analytics.

tools.name: Paved
tools.pricing: Not publicly listed for publishers (advertiser budgets from under $1,000).
tools.best_for: Established newsletters looking for sponsor demand
tools.verdict: A large newsletter ad network. Advertisers want audience size and data, so it suits writers with a sizable list.

tools.name: Hecto
tools.pricing: Marketplace; creators list ad packages with upfront prices (platform pricing on its site).
tools.best_for: Selling sponsorship slots with transparent, upfront prices
tools.verdict: A straightforward sponsorship marketplace. Listing is easy, but demand varies by niche.

tools.name: Swapstack
tools.pricing: Pricing not listed on the homepage.
tools.best_for: Finding sponsors and affiliate deals for small and mid-sized newsletters
tools.verdict: One of the original newsletter sponsorship marketplaces. Worth a free signup to see what deals match your niche.

tools.name: Gumroad
tools.pricing: No monthly fee; 10% + $0.50 per transaction on direct sales.
tools.best_for: Selling ebooks, templates and guides alongside your newsletter
tools.verdict: The simplest way to sell a digital product to your readers. Fees are high per sale but there's no fixed cost.

tools.name: Ko-fi
tools.pricing: Free with a 5% platform fee on some features; Ko-fi Gold $12/mo for 0% platform fee.
tools.best_for: One-off tips from readers who won't commit to a paid subscription
tools.verdict: A low-friction tip jar that complements paid subscriptions.
